areaCheck.method: Official land area (ALAND) of each identically numbered district compared between the 119th Congress cartographic boundary file and the 120th Congress TIGER/Line files, in states the Census Bureau reports as unchanged.

congress120.note: On September 23, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court declined to allow Missouri to use a new congressional map for the 2026 elections that had been created under House Bill 1 of the 103rd General Assembly’s 2nd Extraordinary Session and signed by the Governor in September 2025. This paused an order from a federal appeals court directing the state to use the new map. Prior to this decision, the U.S. Census Bureau had collected the new congressional map from the state and generated some products based on that new plan. All of these products have now been regenerated. Block Equivalency Files were regenerated and posted on October 7, 2026. As of November 10, 2026 TIGER/Line GeoPackages, Geodatabases and Shapefiles were also regenerated. Users who previously downloaded these products prior to their regeneration should download the updated versions available below. The Missouri plan now remains unchanged from the plans used in the 2022 and 2024 elections.
congress120.quote: Nine states (Alabama, California, Florida, Louisiana, North Carolina, Ohio, Tennessee, Texas, and Utah) delineated new boundaries for the 2026 election cycle
congress120.unchangedQuote: All other states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico had no changes to their congressional district boundaries from the 2024 cycle.

populationAvailability.cd120: Not yet published by the Census Bureau. For states the Bureau reports as unchanged, the 119th Congress figures describe identical districts.
